To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consumers’ perceived risk of online shopping is a significant factor in determining their attitude towards online purchasing and their online purchasing behaviour in Malaysia.
consumers’ perceived risk of online shopping has significant impact on their attitude and online purchasing behaviour.

consumers’ attitude towards online shopping is positively influenced by convenience risk and negatively influenced by product risk, financial risk and non-delivery risk, while online purchasing behaviour is significantly influenced by attitude towards online shopping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between consumers’ perceived risk and online purchasing behaviour.
the impact of perceived risk on online shopping behaviour, which has not been studied before.
the relationship among consumers’ perceived risks, attitude and online purchasing behaviour in the context of online shopping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
online buyers are willing to purchase products from the online marketplace, but they are still concerned on product risk, financial risk, non-delivery risk and the convenience risk.
consumers’ perceived risk has negative effect on consumers’ purchasing intention.
consumers’ attitude towards online shopping is positively affected by convenience risk and negatively affected by product risk, financial risk and non-delivery risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers are more likely to shop online if they have positive attitude towards online shopping.
the study has provided a better understanding of the relationship among perceived risk, attitude, and online purchasing behaviour.

the findings of the study are useful to the online sellers and online marketplace to understand consumers’ perceived risk towards online shopping, and to manage and reduce the risks in order to increase consumers’ attitude towards online shopping.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perceived risk of online shopping can be mitigated by providing consumers a safe and secure online purchasing platform.
the risk perception of consumers is the most critical factor to influence their online shopping behaviour.
the perceived risk factors have significant influence on consumers attitude, which in turn influence the online purchasing behavior.
